body: On the other hand wouldn't that penalize newer browsers as they would have to include unrequired polyfills/facades ?
+1 to vicb comment. If you need the functionality, you might as well provide the shim yourself?

If the user targets a runtime where more APIs are available, they can bring
typings for those.
But Angular's usage of these APIs forces all users to target such
environments or shim the behavior.
I think Rado knows better why we don't just bundle es6-shim with angular...

+1 for not using ES6 features in angular. User can always decide, but we should not force.
I guess I'm not clear on the alternative. Provide custom implementations? Doesn't that bloat the source size just as much as shimming?

Just don't use the new APIs. Note that we can use ES6 syntax that
TypeScript de-sugars, just not things that require runtime shims. Evan, is
there a particular API you think we should be using?
